questions.question: How many crores did the Union Government approve to the States for FY 2026–27 as Finance Commission Grants as recommended by the 16th Finance Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1.4 lakh crore.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **The Union Budget 2026-27 allocated ₹1.4 lakh crore to States as Finance Commission Grants as recommended by the 16th Finance Commission.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The amount of ₹1.4 lakh crore is specifically provided for Finance Commission Grants in FY 2026-27.**
 
• This allocation follows recommendations made by the 16th Finance Commission.
 
• Finance Commission Grants support State budgets for development and welfare expenditure.
 
• The grants aim to improve fiscal federalism and financial stability across States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Finance Commission Grants__

 __
 
• Grants provided by the Union Government to States based on Finance Commission recommendations.
 
• They help bridge revenue gaps and support key sectors like health, education and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• 16th Finance Commission__
 __
 
• An independent constitutional body that recommends fiscal devolution and grants to States.
 
• Its recommendations guide the distribution of central funds to improve equity and efficiency.
 
 
 
• Fiscal Federalism__
 __
 
• Refers to financial relations between central and state governments.
 
• Grants and revenue sharing help balance disparities across regions.
 
 
 
• Lakh Crore__
 
 
• “Lakh crore” is a unit used in Indian financial reporting.
 
• 1 lakh crore equals 1,00,000 crore.

questions.question: What is the main focus of the Tribes Advisory Council (TAC) in Jharkhand?

options.text: To improve educational standards in tribal areas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To address tribal welfare issues**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tribes Advisory Council (TAC) is a statutory body established under the **Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The primary focus of the TAC is to **safeguard the rights and promote the welfare of Scheduled Tribes** in states where they are significantly present.
 
• In Jharkhand, the TAC plays a critical role in **advising the state government** on matters related to the welfare and advancement of tribal communities.
 
• The council addresses issues such as **land rights, education, healthcare, and employment opportunities** for tribal populations.
 
• It also monitors the implementation of **tribal-specific policies and development programs** to ensure equitable growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fifth Schedule of the Constitution:** It provides for the establishment of Tribes Advisory Councils in states with significant tribal populations to ensure their protection and development.
 
• **Jharkhand's Tribal Population:** Jharkhand is home to 32 recognized Scheduled Tribes, including Santhals, Oraons, Mundas, and Ho tribes, who form a substantial percentage of the state's population.
 
• **PESA Act:** The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, empowers tribal communities by recognizing their traditional governance systems and granting them control over resources in their areas.
 
• **Issues Addressed by TAC:** Key areas include preventing alienation of tribal lands, improving access to education and healthcare, addressing unemployment, and preserving cultural heritage.
 
• **Role of TAC in Policy Implementation:** The council ensures that state policies align with constitutional provisions and tribal welfare goals, acting as a bridge between tribal communities and the government.

questions.question: Who among the following is not a member of a high level committee constituted on simultaneous elections?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Tushar Mehta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Simultaneous elections** refer to holding elections for the Lok Sabha and all State Assemblies simultaneously. This concept is being widely discussed in India to ensure electoral efficiency and reduce frequent disruptions due to elections.
 
• The government constituted a high-level committee to explore the feasibility and framework for conducting simultaneous elections. The committee includes legal, administrative, and constitutional experts.
 
• **Dr. Niten Chandra, Dr. Subhash C. Kashyap, and Sri N.K. Singh** are members of the committee. They bring expertise in constitutional law, governance, and public finance, respectively. *Hence, these individuals are part of the committee.*
 
• However, **Sri Tushar Mehta**, the current Solicitor General of India, is **not a member** of this high-level committee. His role primarily involves representing the government in legal matters and is unrelated to this committee. *Hence, option 3 is correct.*
 
• The committee's purpose is to explore legal, logistical, and constitutional frameworks to implement simultaneous elections while ensuring democratic principles are upheld. *Thus, Sri Tushar Mehta is not involved in this task.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Simultaneous Elections:**

 
 
• **Concept:** Simultaneous elections aim to synchronize Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections to reduce costs, streamline governance, and minimize political disruptions.
 
• **Challenges:** Implementing simultaneous elections requires constitutional amendments, political consensus, logistical preparation, and effective voter awareness campaigns.
 
• **Historical Background:** India practiced simultaneous elections until **1967**. However, due to premature dissolution of assemblies and other factors, this practice was discontinued.
 
 
 
• **Role of the High-Level Committee:**
 
 
• **Purpose:** To examine the feasibility of simultaneous elections and suggest necessary amendments or frameworks.
 
• **Key Members:** Include experts like **Dr. Subhash C. Kashyap** (Constitutional expert), **Dr. Niten Chandra** (Legal Secretary), and **Sri N.K. Singh** (Economist).
 
 
 
• **Sri Tushar Mehta:**
 
 
• **Designation:** Solicitor General of India. His role is primarily focused on representing the government in legal cases.
 
• **Not a Member:** Despite his legal expertise, he is not part of the high-level committee for simultaneous elections.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**

 
 
• **Articles 83, 85, 172, and 174** may need amendments to ensure synchronization of elections. These articles govern the tenure and dissolution of legislatures.
 
• Past committees, including the **Law Commission**, have recommended simultaneous elections to reduce election-related disruptions.
 
 
 
• **Historical Instances:**
 
 
• **1967:** Simultaneous elections were held until this year. Post-1967, political instability led to the practice being discontinued.
 
• **Recent Discussions:** The idea has been revived in recent years as part of efforts to streamline governance and reduce election costs.

questions.question: Which one of the following chaired the High-Level Working Group constituted to examine the recommendations relating to the ecological management of the Western Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

**__Key Points__**
__
• **Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel (WGEEP): **This earlier panel was chaired by **Madhav Gadgil** and made recommendations on conservation and ecological regulation in the Western Ghats.

• **High-Level Working Group (HLWG): **After the Gadgil panel report, the Government constituted a **High-Level Working Group** to examine its recommendations. This HLWG was chaired by **Dr. K. Kasturirangan**.

• **Option A: Sunita Narain** did not chair this High-Level Working Group. Hence, **Option A is incorrect**.

• **Option B: Madhav Gadgil** chaired the earlier **Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel**, not the later High-Level Working Group constituted to examine its recommendations. Hence, **Option B is incorrect**.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Kasturirangan Committee** was constituted later to review and examine the Gadgil panel’s recommendations.

• The Western Ghats are recognized as a major **biodiversity hotspot** and a region of high ecological sensitivity.

• Much of the policy discussion focused on identifying **Ecologically Sensitive Areas (ESAs)** and balancing **conservation** with **livelihood and development concerns**.

questions.question: A Committee was constituted to formulate fundamental duties after emergency in 1976. It was headed by which of the following personalities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sardar Swaran Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The committee to recommend the incorporation of **Fundamental Duties** into the Indian Constitution was formed after the **National Emergency of 1975-77**.
 
• **Sardar Swaran Singh**, a senior Congress leader and former Union Minister, was appointed as the head of this committee. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• The recommendations of the committee led to the inclusion of **Part IVA (Article 51A)** in the Indian Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were influenced by the concepts of duties found in the **USSR Constitution**. This was seen as a way to balance citizens' rights with their responsibilities toward the nation.
 
• The committee emphasized that every citizen has certain moral obligations towards the nation, which should be constitutionally recognized to promote a sense of duty and discipline.
 
• The original list of Fundamental Duties included **10 duties**, which were later expanded to **11** by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are listed under **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution. They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
• The duties aim to remind citizens of their responsibilities toward the nation, society, and fellow citizens, promoting harmony and patriotism.
 
• Examples include respecting the **National Flag** and the **National Anthem**, protecting the environment, and safeguarding public property.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• This is often referred to as the **“Mini-Constitution”** due to the extensive changes it introduced, including the addition of Fundamental Duties.
 
• It also added terms like **“Socialist”** and **“Secular”** to the Preamble and gave precedence to the Directive Principles of State Policy over Fundamental Rights in certain cases.
 
 
 
• **Sardar Swaran Singh:**
 
 
• Sardar Swaran Singh was a prominent political leader in India, serving as the **External Affairs Minister** and holding various other portfolios in the Union Cabinet.
 
• He was known for his role in formulating key policies and was instrumental in drafting recommendations for the Fundamental Duties.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Current List of Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• The 11 Fundamental Duties include respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, and safeguarding public property.
 
• The 11th duty, added by the **86th Amendment Act, 2002**, requires parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children aged between **6 and 14 years**.
 
 
 
• **Non-Enforceability of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• Though non-justiciable, the Fundamental Duties serve as a moral and ethical guideline for citizens.
 
• Courts may refer to these duties when interpreting laws or resolving cases involving public interest.

questions.question: Under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), entities that exceed their specified emission reduction targets can generate carbon credits. Who is the designated Regulator for the CCTS scheme, responsible for regulatory oversight and enforcement?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)** was officially notified by the **Ministry of Power** in **June 2023** under the powers conferred by the **Energy Conservation Act, 2001**.

• Under the provisions of this scheme, the **Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC)** is designated as the **Regulator**. It is tasked with the critical responsibility of providing **regulatory oversight** and enforcement for the trading of **Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs)**.

• The **CERC** ensures that the trading platform operates with transparency and efficiency, safeguarding the market against manipulation while facilitating the exchange of credits between entities.

• The scheme aims to create a robust **Indian Carbon Market (ICM)** where 'obligated entities' that exceed their emission reduction targets can sell credits to those that fall short, thereby incentivizing **decarbonization**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)**:

• BEE serves as the **Administrator** for the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme.

• Its functions include identifying sectors, developing **emission targets**, and recommending the issuance of **Carbon Credit Certificates** to the Ministry.

• **Grid Controller of India Limited**:

• This organization acts as the **Registry** for the scheme.

• It is responsible for maintaining a comprehensive database, tracking the **lifecycle of credits** (issuance, transfer, and surrender), and managing the accounts of registered entities.

• **Objectives of CCTS**:

• The primary objective is to help India achieve its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the **Paris Agreement**.

• It facilitates the reduction of **Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions** by putting a financial value on carbon, thereby encouraging investments in **green technology** and **renewable energy**.

</ul

questions.question: The Estimates committee of the Indian Parliament consists of:

options.text: Both the members of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
Elected Members of Rajya Sabha only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Members of Lok Sabha only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Estimates Committee of the Indian Parliament is composed exclusively of **members from the Lok Sabha**.
 
• This committee consists of **30 members**, who are elected annually by the Lok Sabha from among its members.
 
• **Rajya Sabha members are not part of the Estimates Committee**, as it is solely a Lok Sabha body.
 
• The role of the committee is to examine the estimates included in the budget and suggest economies in public expenditure.
 
• The Estimates Committee was first established in **1950** and plays a pivotal role in ensuring financial discipline and accountability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Composition of Committees in Parliament:**

 
 
• The Indian Parliament has various standing and ad hoc committees, each with specific roles in legislative and financial oversight.
 
• Committees like the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) and Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) include members from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• However, the Estimates Committee is unique as it comprises only Lok Sabha members.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Estimates Committee:**
 
 
• To examine the budget estimates presented to Parliament.
 
• To suggest alternative policies for achieving the desired objectives at lower costs.
 
• To ensure that money is spent judiciously and efficiently by government departments.
 
 
 
• **Election of Members:**
 
 
• Members of the Estimates Committee are elected by the Lok Sabha through a system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• The Chairperson of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Committees' Role:**
 
 
• They provide detailed scrutiny of legislative proposals, budgets, and policies, which is often not possible in plenary sessions of Parliament.
 
• Committees like the Estimates Committee ensure financial accountability and transparency in governance.

questions.question: The committee formed to recommend financial sector reforms after 1991 was the ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narasimham Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Narasimham Committee was constituted in 1991 under the chairmanship of **M. Narasimham**, a former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• The committee was tasked with recommending reforms for **India's financial sector**, focusing on banking, monetary policy, and fiscal management.
 
• Key recommendations included **reducing government ownership in public sector banks**, allowing more autonomy, and encouraging private sector participation.
 
• The committee emphasized the need for the establishment of **prudential norms** for asset classification, income recognition, and provisioning for bad debts.
 
• It also proposed the **creation of a competitive and efficient banking system** by reducing non-performing assets (NPAs) and improving the capital adequacy ratio.
 
• The Narasimham Committee played a pivotal role in shaping India's financial landscape and ushering in **liberalization and privatization** of the banking sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urjit Patel Committee**

 
 
• This committee was formed under former RBI Governor **Urjit Patel** in 2013 to review and strengthen India's monetary policy framework.
 
• It recommended moving towards a **Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT)** framework with a target inflation rate of 4% (+/- 2%).
 
• The committee emphasized the need for an autonomous monetary policy committee (MPC) to oversee inflation targets and economic stability.
 
• Its recommendations led to the adoption of the **inflation-targeting framework** by the RBI under the amended RBI Act, 1934.
 
 
 
• **Shanta Kumar Committee**
 
 
• This committee, led by Shanta Kumar, was formed in 2014 to suggest reforms in India's **Food Corporation of India (FCI)**.
 
• The key recommendations included restructuring FCI, improving foodgrain storage, and reducing wastage.
 
• It proposed transferring the management of foodgrain procurement and distribution to states and focusing on the efficiency of public distribution systems (PDS).
 
• The committee aimed to enhance the overall food security architecture in India.
 
 
 
• **P.J. Nayak Committee**
 
 
• The P.J. Nayak Committee was constituted in 2014 to review governance in India's **public sector banks (PSBs)**.
 
• It recommended the establishment of a **Bank Investment Company (BIC)** to oversee the government’s investments in PSBs.
 
• The committee emphasized giving PSBs greater operational autonomy and reducing government interference.
 
• It suggested reforms in the appointment process of PSB board members and improving accountability measures.

• Dr. S. Jaishankar is the current Union Minister of External Affairs and was not involved in the High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections.

• **Jagat Prakash Nadda**

• **Simultaneous Elections**
 
 
• The concept of simultaneous elections refers to holding elections for the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies at the same time.
 
• The idea aims to reduce the costs and administrative burden associated with frequent elections in India.
 
• It requires significant amendments to the Constitution and election laws, along with consensus among political parties.

questions.question: Which one of the following Parliamentary Committees has no representation from 'Rajya Sabha'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Estimates Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Estimates Committee is unique to the Lok Sabha and has **no representation from the Rajya Sabha**.
 
• It was first constituted in **1950**, based on the recommendations of the John Mathai Committee.
 
• The main function of the Estimates Committee is to **examine the budget estimates** and suggest ways to improve the efficiency of government expenditure.
 
• The committee consists of **30 members**, all of whom are elected by the Lok Sabha members from amongst themselves annually.
 
• As the Rajya Sabha does not participate in the election of its members, the Estimates Committee is solely composed of Lok Sabha members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary Committees**: These are committees appointed or elected by the House or nominated by the Speaker and work under the control of the presiding officer. They play a crucial role in the legislative process by scrutinizing bills, budgets, and policies.
 
• **Public Accounts Committee (PAC)**: This committee examines the accounts showing the appropriation of funds granted by Parliament and ensures public money is spent in accordance with Parliament's decisions. It includes members from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• **Committee on Public Undertakings**: This committee evaluates the performance of public sector enterprises and includes members from both Houses of Parliament.
 
• **Library Committee**: This committee advises on matters related to the Parliament Library and includes members from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• **Financial Committees**: The three significant financial committees of Parliament are the Estimates Committee, Public Accounts Committee, and Committee on Public Undertakings. Of these, only the Estimates Committee does not include members from the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Which committee was set up by a government of India in January 2000 to suggest the structural changes in the police to meet the challenges in the new millennium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padmanabhaiah Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Padmanabhaiah Committee was set up by the Government of India in **January 2000** to recommend structural reforms in the police system.
 
• The committee's primary objective was to **modernize the police force** and enable it to meet the emerging challenges of the **new millennium**.
 
• It emphasized the need for **accountability, transparency, and efficiency** in the functioning of the police to address contemporary issues like terrorism, cybercrime, and organized crime.
 
• The committee proposed several reforms, including the creation of a **National Security Commission** and greater coordination between the police and intelligence agencies.
 
• The recommendations also focused on improving **training and infrastructure** for the police force and ensuring a citizen-friendly approach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gore Committee**

 
 
• This committee was established in the 1970s to review police training methods and suggest improvements.
 
• It focused on **human resource development** within the police force.
 
• It emphasized the importance of behavioral training and professional ethics for law enforcement personnel.
 
 
 
• **Ribeiro Committee**
 
 
• Set up in the 1990s, this committee was tasked with **reviewing police reforms**.
 
• It recommended measures to enhance **police autonomy** and reduce political interference in policing matters.
 
 
 
• **Malimath Committee**
 
 
• Formed in 2000, this committee focused on **reforms in the criminal justice system** in India.
 
• It suggested changes to ensure **speedy justice** and strengthen the prosecution system.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by the Police in Modern Times**
 
 
• Emerging crimes like **cybercrime** and **terrorism** require advanced training and technology.
 
• Lack of adequate resources, infrastructure, and manpower hampers efficient policing.
 
• Ensuring a balance between **law enforcement** and **citizen rights** remains a critical challenge.

questions.question: Who was the chairman of the Second Commission on centre-state relations set-up by the government of India in April 2007?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M.M. Punchhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Commission on Centre-State Relations was set up by the Government of India in **April 2007** to address evolving dynamics between the central and state governments.
 
• **Justice M.M. Punchhi**, a former Chief Justice of India, was appointed as the chairman of this commission.
 
• The commission was tasked with reviewing the existing arrangements and suggesting measures for efficient governance and cooperative federalism in India.
 
• The **Justice M.M. Punchhi Commission** submitted its final report to the government in **March 2010**.
 
• The recommendations of the commission covered critical areas such as national security, financial relations, and constitutional governance to strengthen federal principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centre-State Relations:**

 
 
• Centre-State relations in India are categorized into three areas: Legislative, Administrative, and Financial relations.
 
• The aim is to ensure a balance of power and smooth functioning of governance in a federal setup.
 
• Articles 245 to 263 of the Indian Constitution deal with legislative and administrative relations, while financial relations are covered under Articles 268 to 293.
 
 
 
• **First Commission on Centre-State Relations:**
 
 
• Headed by Justice R.S. Sarkaria, the first commission was established in June 1983 and submitted its report in 1988.
 
• It examined and recommended measures for restructuring centre-state relations to ensure smooth governance.
 
• Key recommendations included the proper use of Article 356, strengthening the Inter-State Council, and revisiting the role of the Finance Commission.
 
 
 
• **Key Recommendations of the Punchhi Commission:**
 
 
• Suggested clear guidelines for the imposition of President's Rule under Article 356 to prevent its misuse.
 
• Recommended that national interest should guide the deployment of central forces in states.
 
• Proposed reforms in the role and functioning of the Governor to maintain impartiality.
 
• Called for a permanent Interstate Trade and Commerce Commission to resolve disputes between states.
 
 
 
• **Cooperative Federalism:**
 
 
• Cooperative federalism emphasizes collaboration between the central and state governments for collective progress and development.
 
• In India, mechanisms like the NITI Aayog, Inter-State Council, and GST Council promote cooperative federalism.

questions.question: The NK Singh Committee, which was formed in 2016, was associated with which of the following?

options.text: Reviewing the trade deficit in India

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Reviewing the FRBM Act, 2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **NK Singh Committee** was set up in **2016** to review the provisions of the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003**.
 
• The **FRBM Act, 2003**, was enacted by the Indian Government to ensure **fiscal discipline** and reduce fiscal deficits.
 
• The Committee, chaired by **NK Singh**, aimed to make recommendations on revising the fiscal roadmap in light of **changing macroeconomic conditions**.
 
• It proposed introducing a new framework for fiscal policy, focusing on **debt and deficit targets**, and recommended specific **escape clauses** for unforeseen situations like natural disasters or economic crises.
 
• The Committee suggested setting a target for the **government’s debt-to-GDP ratio** and recommended measures for better **transparency and accountability** in fiscal management.
 
• It emphasized the importance of fiscal discipline for **economic stability** and long-term growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Introduction of Standing Deposit Facility**__

 __
 
• The **Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)** is a monetary tool introduced by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to manage liquidity in the banking system.
 
• The SDF allows the RBI to absorb excess funds from banks without requiring the collateral that is typically needed in open market operations.
 
• The SDF was not related to the NK Singh Committee but was part of broader measures in monetary policy frameworks.
 
 
 
• **Reviewing the trade deficit in India**__
 __
 
• The term **trade deficit** refers to a situation where a country's imports exceed its exports.
 
• Trade deficit reviews are generally conducted by the **Ministry of Commerce** or related economic bodies, not by the NK Singh Committee.
 
 
 
• **Introduction of Monetary Policy Committee**__
 
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** was established in **2016** under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, to set the policy interest rates.
 
• The MPC is composed of six members, including three from the RBI and three external experts appointed by the Government of India.
 
• This was a separate initiative and not related to the NK Singh Committee.

questions.question: Which of the following commissions was appointed to look into the question of states based on language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhar Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dhar Commission was appointed in **1948** by the Government of India to examine the feasibility of reorganizing states on a linguistic basis.
 
• The Commission, chaired by Justice **S.K. Dhar**, recommended that the reorganization of states should not be solely based on language but also consider administrative convenience and economic viability.
 
• The Dhar Commission argued that linguistic reorganization could potentially disrupt national unity and lead to administrative complications.
 
• The findings of the Dhar Commission were opposed by linguistic groups, leading to the formation of subsequent committees like the JVP Committee in 1949.
 
• Despite its recommendations, the demand for linguistic states continued, eventually culminating in the formation of the first linguistic state, Andhra Pradesh, in 1953.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gadgil Commission**

 
 
• The Gadgil Commission, officially known as the **Committee on Plan Projects**, was established in 1960 and focused on development planning in India.
 
• The Commission is primarily associated with recommending the **Gadgil Formula**, which allocates financial resources to states based on population, per capita income, and other factors.
 
 
 
• **Sarkaria Commission**
 
 
• The Sarkaria Commission was constituted in **1983** to review the **Center-State relations** in India.
 
• It focused on the distribution of powers between the Union and State governments and suggested measures to improve coordination and cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee**
 
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was set up in **1976** to recommend changes to the Constitution of India.
 
• It is best known for its recommendations on incorporating the **Fundamental Duties** of citizens into the Constitution, which were added as Part IV-A by the 42nd Amendment.
